newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan recovery trend goes on despite tax rise--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan recovery trend goes on despite tax rise--BOJ.

text.p: Japan's overall economy is continuing on a gradual recovery trend, on the back of firm production and income growth, despite a lingering impact from an increase in the consumption tax, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Thursday.
Public-sector investment and housing investment are on a declining trend but net exports are continuing to increase, Matsushita told a conference of regional bankers.

Although there is a lingering impact on private consumption from the April 1 rise in the sales tax, especially on purchases of durable goods, the employment and income situation is still gradually improving, he said.
"I believe that the recovery trend (in consumption) has not been damaged," Matsushita said.

Although the pace of improvement in the profits of smaller non-manufacturing firms is flagging at the moment, the overall trend of rising profits is being maintained. In this environment, corporate capital spending is steadily increasing, Matsushita said.
Production has continued to rise since late last year and has been steady since the spring, he added.
A positive cyclical mechanism in the private-sector economy continues to function.

"The slowdown in the economy now will be temporary, and there is a high possibility that the economy will continue its recovery. However, we must keep sufficient watch over these points, including the speed of the recovery," he said.
Prices are generally stable if one excludes the impact from the rise in the consumption tax, Matsushita said.
"Monetary policy management for now will put an emphasis on making the basis for economic recovery firmer while keeping a close watch over developments," he said.

The disposal of problem loans remains an extremely important issue for Japan's financial system, he said, adding that the central bank will put in maximum efforts to regain the credibility of the financial system both at home and abroad.

Although some financial institutions are being investigated for possible violations of the commercial code, the BOJ hopes better management and a clarification of the facts will make the industry in Japan more credible.
"We plan to push for stronger overall risk management at financial institutions, including their credit-extending businesses and internal management," Matsushita said.
